newsitem.title: LATVIA: Latvia says meets World Bank energy debt process.
newsitem.headline: Latvia says meets World Bank energy debt process.

text.p: The Latvian finance ministry on Thursday said the Baltic state was meeting the demands of the World Bank on sorting out its energy sector debt problems.

A solution to the debts in the energy sector is vital for Latvia to access a further $40 million of World Bank structural reform credits. The government decided to take debt off the balance sheets of energy firms and collect the funds itself.

"Latvia fulfills World Bank demands on energy utilities' debts by the government taking on the solving of the debts of Latvian Gas," finance ministry deputy state secretary Inguna Sudraba told a news conference.
Latvia has already qualified for $20 million of the credit but has to meet further requirements for the following tranche. It has not drawn down any of the loan.
The $40 million tranche will be used to repay a Nomura eurbond that was launched in 1995 in the wake of a bank crisis and is due for repayment this year.

Another condition for getting the second tranche is that some two to three percent of GDP should be earmarked for investment and that funds already set aside for investment should not be used for other purposes.
Additional resources for helping to rationalise spending on administration should also be set aside, Sudraba added.
